anomaly_def.Name: Schema and Index Design Anomaly + Query Plan Selection Anomaly + Storage Space Capacity Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Schema and Index Design Anomaly : Static mismatch between physical data model (tables, indexes, partitions, datatypes, constraints) and workload access patterns forces inherently inefficient access paths.
Query Plan Selection Anomaly : Optimizer chooses a sub-optimal execution strategy despite reasonably accurate statistics, yielding plans that diverge from the cost-efficient options available.
Storage Space Capacity Anomaly : Free space in data files, logs, temp areas, or backups approaches hard limits, risking allocation failures and blocking DML or query processing.

When all three root causes co-exist, the workload may exhibit runaway I/O and CPU consumption from full-table scans or non-covering index probes, frequent plan flip-flops, explosive temporary-space usage for sorts and hash joins, and accelerated growth of tables, indexes, and redo/undo logs. Operators may observe simultaneous query slowdowns, spike-shaped latency patterns, sudden "out of space" or "cannot allocate extent" errors, aborted batch jobs, and cascaded stalls as log files, temp segments, or archive destinations saturate. The overlapping symptoms make it difficult to isolate any single culprit because design flaws, bad plans, and space exhaustion each manifest in similar performance degradations.

Causally, missing or sub-optimal indexes and inappropriate partitioning inflate table and index sizes and force the optimizer to pick heavier plans (e.g., full scans or large hash joins). Even when selective paths exist, the plan-selection anomaly can disregard them, compounding the I/O footprint generated by the design flaw. The enlarged working set and higher redo/undo generation accelerate space consumption in data, temp, and log areas; once space becomes scarce, auto-extension failures or log-archive back-pressure further degrade plan performance by disabling parallelism, spilling to disk sooner, or triggering statement aborts. Conversely, near-full tablespaces may cause extent fragmentation that degrades index efficiency and influences the optimizer’s cost model, increasing the likelihood of sub-optimal plans. Thus, each root cause perpetuates the others, leading to a feedback loop of worsening performance, erratic plan behavior, and eventual space-related outages.

entry.official_definition: The number of seconds to wait for more data from a connection before aborting the read.
entry.trigger_condition: The server waits for additional data from a connection longer than net_read_timeout.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL server system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
